nodes.subject: audio codec
nodes.object: digital audio to reduce storage or transmission bandwidth while retaining quality

support_spans.exact_quote: An audio codec is a device or computer program capable of encoding or decoding a digital data stream (a codec ) that encodes or decodes audio .
The objective of the algorithm is to represent the high-fidelity audio signal with a minimum number of bits while retaining quality.

accepted_phrases: An audio codec encodes or decodes an audio stream, and software codecs compress and decompress digital audio to reduce storage or transmission bandwidth while retaining quality.

nodes.subject: ABX listening comparison
nodes.object: whether a perceptual difference can be reliably identified under the test circumstances

support_spans.exact_quote: An ABX test is a method of comparing two choices of sensory stimuli to identify detectable differences between them.

If X cannot be identified reliably with a low p-value in a predetermined number of trials, then the null hypothesis cannot be rejected and it cannot be proven that there is a perceptible difference between A and B.
Thus, the ABX test answers whether or not, under the test circumstances, a perceptual difference can be found.

accepted_phrases: ABX compares known A and B with a randomized X and requires reliable identification in predetermined trials before claiming a perceptible difference under the test circumstances.

nodes.subject: codec listening test
nodes.object: double-blind comparison and similar or identical bitrates for meaningful codec performance comparison

support_spans.exact_quote: Most tests take the form of a double-blind comparison.

To obtain meaningful results, listening tests must compare codecs' performance at similar or identical bitrates , since the audio quality produced by any lossy encoder will be trivially improved by increasing the bitrate.
If listeners cannot consistently distinguish a lossy encoder's output from the uncompressed original audio, then it may be concluded that the codec has achieved transparency .

accepted_phrases: Meaningful codec listening tests commonly use double-blind comparison and similar or identical bitrates; consistent inability to distinguish from the original supports transparency for that test.

nodes.subject: auditory masking
nodes.object: perception and the threshold of a target sound in the presence of masking noise

support_spans.exact_quote: In audio signal processing , auditory masking occurs when the perception of one sound is affected by the presence of another sound.
The masked threshold is the quietest level of the signal perceived when combined with a specific masking noise.

accepted_phrases: Auditory masking occurs when one sound affects perception of another, and a target's masked threshold is measured in the presence of a specific masking noise.
